visualCharacteristics.purpose: insights article page header: feature image with an overlapping white panel holding tags, title, intro, byline and share links
traits: white panel overlapping the bottom of the image at desktop
tag chips linking to tag pages above the H1
share links (Facebook, X, LinkedIn, email, copy link)
optional header video over the feature image (muted loop, pause/play button), the image as poster and fallback

contentPattern.structure: 1 column. Row 1: feature image (alt required), optionally a link to the header video (/content/dam/...mp4, " {mobile}" after it to play below 768px). Row 2: H1 and intro paragraph(s). Tags, publication date, reading time and author are NOT authored in the block; they come from page metadata: tags (comma separated, rendered as chips linking to /<country>/<lang>/articles/tags/<slug-of-tag>), publication-date (ISO date like 2026-08-20 or a unix timestamp, formatted per page locale; other text is shown as authored), reading-time (shown as authored, e.g. '7 min read') and author; the byline reads 'date | reading time | author' and omits missing parts. Share links for Facebook, X, LinkedIn, email and a copy-link button use the current page URL. UI strings have English and German defaults by page language and can be overridden with optional two-cell rows: Tags label (Tags / Schlagwörter), Share label (Share this article / Artikel teilen), Facebook label, X label, LinkedIn label, Email label (Email / E-Mail), Copy link label (Copy link / Link kopieren), Link copied label (Link copied / Link kopiert). Defensive: the first picture is the image, the first heading the title, paragraphs after it the intro; a missing image renders the panel without the image.

usage: First block on every insights article page (/de/en/articles/...), e.g. /de/en/articles/explore-the-world/eat-see-do-berlin.
reuseGuidance: Use only as the article page header. Keep tags, publication-date, reading-time and author in page metadata so related-articles and listings can read them from the query index.
